content.headline: Bottom Trawling: Dragging Coastal Communities Into Crisis
content.body:
Billions of people rely on fish for protein, and fishing is the principal livelihood for millions around the world. Yet bottom trawling—the world's most productive fishing method, responsible for over 30 million tonnes of catch annually—is threatening both food security and economic stability in coastal communities.

When fish disappear due to destructive fishing practices, so do jobs and coastal economies. Millions of people in largely developing, coastal communities depend on the fishing industry for their livelihood. Bottom trawling has been widely implicated in the population collapse of numerous fish species worldwide, including orange roughy, barndoor skate, and sharks.

This destructive cycle threatens the long-term sustainability of fisheries and the communities that depend on them. While bottom trawling contributes significantly to global fisheries production, its unsustainable practices jeopardize the very foundation of coastal economies and food systems that sustain billions.
content.instagram_caption:
🌊 The hidden cost of your seafood? Coastal communities paying the price.

Bottom trawling isn't just an environmental issue—it's an economic and social crisis. This destructive fishing method catches over 30 million tonnes annually (more than any other method), but at what cost?

• Billions depend on fish for protein
• Millions rely on fishing for their livelihoods  
• Coastal economies collapse when fish disappear
• Bottom trawling has caused population collapses of species like orange roughy and sharks

When we destroy fish populations, we destroy communities. Sustainable fishing isn't just about conservation—it's about protecting jobs, food security, and coastal ways of life.

#BottomTrawling #SustainableFishing #CoastalCommunities #FoodSecurity #OceanConservation #SaveOurSeas
content.call_to_action: Demand sustainable fishing practices that protect both our oceans and coastal communities. Support fisheries that prioritize long-term sustainability over short-term profits. Your choices as a consumer can help preserve livelihoods and food security for millions.
